question: Who among the following devised the system of ‘Subsidiary Alliance’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Wellesley.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Wellesley, Governor-General of India from 1798 to 1805, devised the Subsidiary Alliance system in 1798. (सहायक संधि प्रणाली — लॉर्ड वेलेजली)

 

• Under this system, an Indian ruler entering the alliance had to accept a permanent British force within his territory and pay for its maintenance, could not employ any European in his service without British approval, and could not enter into any alliance or make war with another Indian state without the consent of the British.

 

• In return, the British promised to protect the ruler from external and internal threats, and the ruler had to accept a British Resident at his court.

 

• The Nizam of Hyderabad was the first Indian ruler to accept the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wellesley also fought the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799), in which Tipu Sultan was defeated and killed at Srirangapatnam.

 

• States that accepted the Subsidiary Alliance effectively lost control over their foreign policy and defence, becoming dependent on the British.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Canning (Option 2): He was the Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857 and became the first Viceroy of India in 1858.

 

• Lord William Bentinck (Option 3): He is known for the abolition of Sati (1829) and was the first Governor-General of India (unified title created by the Charter Act of 1833).

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 4): He is known for introducing the Doctrine of Lapse.

question: At which Olympics was Kho-Kho featured in an exhibition in the main stadium?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1936.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kho-Kho was showcased as a demonstration/exhibition sport at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, played in the main Olympic stadium before a large international audience. (खो-खो — 1936 बर्लिन ओलंपिक)

 

• Kho-Kho is an ancient tag-based team sport believed to have originated in Maharashtra, traditionally played on a rectangular field with two teams of chasers and runners.

 

• The 1936 exhibition is regarded as one of the earliest international showcases of the sport, and 2036 (100 years later) is being targeted by Kho-Kho bodies as a goal for the sport's Olympic inclusion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kho-Kho Federation of India was established in 1955, and the first National Kho-Kho Championship was held in 1959-60 at Vijayawada.

 

• The inaugural Kho-Kho World Cup was held in New Delhi in January 2025, won by the Indian men's and women's teams.

 

NOTE

 

• 1932 (Option 2): Kho-Kho was not part of the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics.

 

• 2008 (Option 3): No Kho-Kho exhibition was held at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

 

• 2016 (Option 4): No Kho-Kho exhibition was held at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
option_1: Fats and oils get reduced over time and smell bad.
option_2: Fats and oils are oxidised, they become rancid.
option_3: Antioxidants are added to foods containing fats and oil to prevent oxidation.
option_4: Chips manufacturers usually flush bags of chips with Nitrogen to prevent the chips from getting ranicid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fats and oils get reduced over time and smell bad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This statement is incorrect because fats and oils turning bad-smelling over time is caused by oxidation, not reduction. This process is called rancidity. (विकृतगंधिता — ऑक्सीकरण से, अपचयन से नहीं)

 

• Rancidity occurs when fats and oils in food are oxidised on exposure to air, light, or moisture, changing their smell and taste for the worse.

 

• Antioxidants (substances that resist oxidation) are added to foods containing fats and oils to slow down rancidity and extend shelf life.

 

• Manufacturers of chips and similar fried, fatty snacks usually flush the packets with nitrogen gas (an unreactive/inert gas) instead of air, to keep oxygen away from the food and prevent rancidity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rancidity is a topic covered under physical and chemical changes, since oxidation of fats is a chemical change.

 

• Common antioxidants used in the food industry include BHA (Butylated Hydroxyanisole) and BHT (Butylated Hydroxytoluene).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: This statement is factually correct — oxidation of fats and oils does cause rancidity.

 

• Option 3: This statement is factually correct — antioxidants are indeed added to prevent oxidation of fats/oils in food.

 

• Option 4: This statement is factually correct — nitrogen flushing is a standard practice to prevent chips from turning rancid.

question: Hot local wind that flows over north India in summer is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loo is a strong, hot, dry, dusty local wind that blows across the Indo-Gangetic plains of north India during the day in the summer months (April to June). (लू — उत्तर भारत की गर्म शुष्क पवन)

 

• It results from intense heating of the land surface in the north-western plains, and exposure to it can cause heat stroke.

 

• It typically blows from the west/north-west in the afternoon and dies down at night.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Local winds are named differently across the world based on their region, temperature, and season of occurrence.

 

• In India, apart from Loo, Mango showers and Kaal Baisakhi (Nor'westers) are other well-known local weather phenomena.

 

NOTE

 

• Chinook (Option 2): A warm, dry wind that blows down the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains in North America, often melting snow rapidly.

 

• Mango showers (Option 3): Pre-monsoon showers that occur in Kerala and Karnataka, beneficial for the ripening of mangoes.

 

• Purga (Option 4): A cold, violent wind/blizzard associated with the tundra regions of Russia/Siberia.

question: ‘Nuakhai’ is the state festival of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nuakhai (or Nuakhai Bhetghat) is the state agricultural festival of Odisha, especially popular in the western Odisha (Kosal) region. (नुआखाई — ओडिशा)

 

• It marks the welcoming of the new rice harvest of the season; “Nua” means new and “Khai” means food/eating.

 

• It is usually celebrated on Panchami tithi of the lunar month of Bhadrapada (August-September), a day after Ganesh Chaturthi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Odisha include the Rath Yatra at Puri and Kalinga Mahotsav.

 

NOTE

 

• Meghalaya (Option 1): Known for the Wangala festival (Hundred Drums festival) of the Garo tribe.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Known for the harvest festival Pongal.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Known for the festival of Chhath Puja.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits providing of any religious instruction in the educational institutions maintained by the State?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 28.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 28 of the Indian Constitution provides that no religious instruction shall be imparted in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds. (अनुच्छेद 28 — धार्मिक शिक्षा का निषेध)

 

• It falls under the Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28) in Part III of the Constitution.

 

• Institutions administered by the State but established under an endowment or trust that requires religious instruction to be imparted are exempted [Article 28(2)], and no person attending a State-recognised or State-aided institution can be compelled to take part in religious instruction without consent [Article 28(3)].

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

 

• Article 26 gives every religious denomination the freedom to manage its own religious affairs.

 

• Article 27 states that no person can be compelled to pay taxes for the promotion of a particular religion.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 29 (Option 1): Protects the interests of minorities, giving them the right to conserve their distinct language, script or culture.

 

• Article 30 (Option 3): Gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

 

• Article 31 (Option 4): Originally dealt with the right to property; it was repealed by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.

question: As per the definition of Census of India, a ‘marginal worker’ is a person who works for:
option_1: less than 183 days (or six months) in a year
option_2: more than 183 days (or six months) in a year
solution_text:
The correct answer is less than 183 days (or six months) in a year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India, a ‘marginal worker’ is a person who has worked for less than 183 days (six months) in the reference year. (सीमांत श्रमिक — 183 दिनों से कम)

 

• In contrast, a ‘main worker’ is a person who has worked for 183 days or more (six months or more) in the reference year.

 

• Workers are further classified into cultivators, agricultural labourers, workers in household industry, and other workers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Census also defines ‘non-workers’ as persons who have not been engaged in any economically productive activity during the reference period.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (more than 183 days): This is actually the Census definition of a main worker, not a marginal worker.

 

• Option 3 (eight months): Does not match the Census's 183-day threshold.

 

• Option 4 (83 days): Does not match the Census's 183-day threshold.

question: In which year was the ‘Naye Bharat Ke Sapne’ campaign launched by Meta and the Ministry of Women?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ‘Amrit Generation Campaign: Naye Bharat Ke Sapne’ was launched in 2023 jointly by Meta and the Ministry of Women and Child Development. (नए भारत के सपने अभियान — 2023)

 

• The campaign was aimed at engaging young people to share their vision for India, and to raise awareness on issues such as ending child marriage and promoting gender equality and digital safety.

 

• It used Meta's platforms (Facebook and Instagram) to spread its messaging to the youth of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The campaign was positioned as part of India's journey towards its 100th year of independence (2047), sometimes referred to as ‘Amrit Kaal’.

 

NOTE

 

• 2022, 2020 and 2021 (Options 1, 3 and 4): The campaign was not launched in any of these years; it was launched in 2023.

question: Under which of the following Acts was the power to rule India, transferred from the English East India Company to the British Crown?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act 1858.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred the power to govern India from the East India Company to the British Crown, following the Revolt of 1857. (भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1858 — क्राउन शासन की शुरुआत)

 

• It abolished the Company's Court of Directors and Board of Control, and created the post of Secretary of State for India, responsible to the British Parliament.

 

• The Governor-General of India also became the Viceroy, the Crown's direct representative in India; Lord Canning was the first Viceroy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (first was Lord William Bentinck) and ended the Company's remaining commercial functions.

 

• The Pitt's India Act, 1784 established a system of double government through a Board of Control and the Court of Directors.

 

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first attempt by the British Parliament to regulate the Company's affairs and created the office of Governor-General of Bengal (first was Warren Hastings).

 

NOTE

 

• Charter Act of 1833 (Option 1): Reorganised Company administration but did not transfer power to the Crown.

 

• Regulating Act 1773 (Option 2): Regulated Company affairs; power remained with the Company.

 

• Pitt's India Act 1784 (Option 3): Increased government control over the Company but did not end Company rule.

question: Which of the following is an inactivated (killed) polio vaccine developed in 1952?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salk vaccine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Salk vaccine is an inactivated (killed) polio vaccine (IPV), developed by Dr. Jonas Salk, first tested in 1952 and licensed for use in 1955. (साल्क वैक्सीन — निष्क्रिय पोलियो टीका)

 

• It is administered by injection and uses a killed form of the poliovirus to trigger immunity.

 

• The other major polio vaccine, the Sabin (oral polio) vaccine, uses a live, attenuated virus and is given orally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's polio immunisation programme has used both OPV (Oral Polio Vaccine) and IPV (Inactivated Polio Vaccine).

 

NOTE

 

• Imvanex vaccine (Option 2): A vaccine used against smallpox and mpox (monkeypox), not polio.

 

• HDCV vaccine (Option 3): ‘Human Diploid Cell Vaccine’, used against rabies.

 

• TAB vaccine (Option 4): Used against Typhoid and Paratyphoid A and B.

question: Which of the following statements is correct?.
option_1: The five-year plan focuses mostly on private intervention in the economy.
option_2: The five-year plan always focused on the growth of the tertiary sector.
option_3: The five-year plan permits long-term intervention by the government in the economy.
option_4: A five-year plan always stresses market-oriented activities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The five-year plan permits long-term intervention by the government in the economy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Five-Year Plans were a mechanism for long-term government intervention and planning in the economy, started in 1951 and modelled partly on the Soviet approach. (पंचवर्षीय योजना — दीर्घकालिक सरकारी हस्तक्षेप)

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused primarily on agriculture.

 

• Five-Year Plans were formulated by the Planning Commission, which was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015; the 12th Plan (2012-17) was the last of the series.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India followed a mixed economy model, where both public and private sectors played a role, rather than relying solely on private/market forces.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect — the five-year plans emphasised government/public sector intervention, not mainly private intervention.

 

• Option 2: Incorrect — different plans focused on different sectors (e.g., agriculture, industry) at different times, not always the tertiary sector.

 

• Option 4: Incorrect — five-year plans stressed planned, government-directed development, not purely market-oriented activities.

question: What is the length of Indian Railways network, according to Railway Yearbook 2019-20?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 67,956 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Railway Yearbook 2019-20, the route length of the Indian Railways network was 67,956 km. (भारतीय रेल मार्ग लंबाई — 67,956 किमी)

 

• Route length is distinct from total track length (which includes multiple parallel tracks and yard lines, and is a much larger figure).

 

• The Indian Railways network has grown steadily over the decades — from around 53,596 route km in 1951 to over 68,000 route km in the early 2020s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Railways, headquartered in New Delhi, oversees Indian Railways, which is organised into multiple railway zones.

 

• Indian Railways is among the largest railway networks in the world by route length.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (1,604 km, 63,950 km, 2,402 km): These figures do not match the total route length reported in the Railway Yearbook 2019-20.

question: In Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas yojana, the cost of unit assistance is shared between Central and State Governments in the ratio ___________ in plain areas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 60 : 40.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas Yojana (PMAY-Gramin), the cost of unit assistance for house construction is shared between the Centre and State Governments in the ratio 60:40 in the plains. (प्रधानमंत्री ग्रामीण आवास योजना — मैदानी क्षेत्रों में 60:40 अनुपात)

 

• For North-Eastern and Himalayan States, hilly states, and difficult areas, the ratio is 90:10.

 

• For Union Territories, the entire cost of unit assistance is borne 100% by the Central Government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMAY-Gramin was launched in 2016 (as a restructured version of the earlier Indira Awaas Yojana) under the Ministry of Rural Development, aiming to provide pucca houses to eligible rural households.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (40:60): This is the reverse of the actual ratio and is incorrect.

 

• Option 3 (90:10): This is the ratio applicable to North-Eastern/Himalayan/hilly states, not plain areas.

 

• Option 4 (30:70): This ratio does not apply to PMAY-Gramin.

question: Silappathikaram (the Jewelled Anklet), the earliest epic poem in Tamil was written in the 5th - 6th Century CE by _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ilango Adigal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Silappathikaram (‘The Tale of an Anklet’), the earliest Tamil epic, was composed by Ilango Adigal, a Chera prince believed to be the brother of the Chera king Senguttuvan, around the 5th-6th century CE. (शिलप्पदिकारम् — इलंगो अडिगल)

 

• It is one of the ‘Five Great Epics’ of Tamil literature, along with Manimekalai, Civaka Cintamani, Valayapathi and Kundalakesi.

 

• The epic narrates the story of Kannagi and Kovalan, centred on themes of justice, chastity and morality.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manimekalai, considered a sequel to Silappathikaram, was written by Sittalai Sattanar and has strong Buddhist themes.

 

• Tolkappiyam, the oldest extant Tamil grammar treatise, was written by Tolkappiyar.

 

NOTE

 

• Tolkappiyar (Option 1): Authored the grammar text Tolkappiyam, not Silappathikaram.

 

• Sittalai Sattanar (Option 3): Authored Manimekalai, the sequel epic to Silappathikaram.

 

• Tirumalisai Alwar (Option 4): One of the twelve Alvars, Vaishnavite saint-poets of South India, unrelated to this epic.

question: Which of the following is the largest crustal plate on Earth with an area of over 103,000,000 km²?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific plate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pacific Plate is the largest tectonic (crustal) plate on Earth, with an area of more than 103,000,000 km², covering most of the Pacific Ocean. (प्रशांत प्लेट — सबसे बड़ी विवर्तनिक प्लेट)

 

• Its boundaries largely coincide with the ‘Ring of Fire’, a zone of intense volcanic and seismic activity caused mainly by subduction of the Pacific Plate beneath neighbouring plates.

 

• The plate's interaction with the North American Plate along the San Andreas Fault (a transform boundary) is a well-known example of plate tectonics in action.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The seven major tectonic plates are the African, Antarctic, Eurasian, Indo-Australian, North American, Pacific, and South American plates.

 

NOTE

 

• South American plate (Option 1): A major plate, but much smaller in area than the Pacific Plate.

 

• African plate (Option 2): A major plate, but smaller than the Pacific Plate.

 

• Eurasian plate (Option 3): The largest continental plate (~67 million km²), but still smaller than the Pacific Plate overall.

question: Which of the following personalities is a Padma Shri awardee folk singer from the state of Uttar Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ajita Srivastava.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ajita Srivastava is a well-known Kajri folk singer from Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, and was conferred the Padma Shri (2022) in the field of Art for preserving, conserving and propagating the popular folklore of ‘Kajri’. (अजिता श्रीवास्तव — पद्म श्री, कजरी लोकगायिका)

 

• Kajri is a seasonal folk-song genre of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, traditionally sung during the monsoon season.

 

• She received the award from the then President Ram Nath Kovind.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Teejan Bai is a renowned Pandwani singer from Chhattisgarh and a Padma Vibhushan awardee.

 

• Gurmeet Bawa, often called the ‘Nightingale of Punjab’, was a Punjabi folk singer.

 

NOTE

 

• Ila Arun (Option 1): A well-known Rajasthani folk singer and actress, not from Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Gurmeet Bawa (Option 3): A celebrated Punjabi folk singer, from Punjab, not Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Teejan Bai (Option 4): A Pandwani folk singer from Chhattisgarh, and a Padma Vibhushan (not from UP).

question: Which of the following countries won the first men’s Asian Hockey Championship trophy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pakistan won the first (inaugural) Men's Asian Hockey Championship (Asia Cup), held in 1982 at Karachi. (प्रथम एशियाई हॉकी चैंपियनशिप — पाकिस्तान, 1982)

 

• Pakistan finished the round-robin tournament unbeaten (6 wins out of 6), winning the gold medal.

 

• India finished as the runner-up (silver medal) in that edition, with China taking the bronze medal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tournament, organised under the Asian Hockey Federation, has since come to be widely known as the Hockey Asia Cup.

 

• India has gone on to win the Asia Cup on multiple later occasions, including in 2003, 2007, 2017 and 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Japan (Option 1): Did not win the inaugural 1982 edition.

 

• China (Option 2): Finished third (bronze) in the 1982 edition, not the winner.

 

• India (Option 3): Finished as runner-up (silver) in the inaugural 1982 edition, not champions.

question: Which of the following goods needs further transformation in the economic process?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Intermediate goods.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Intermediate goods are goods used as inputs in the production of other goods and services, and they require further processing/transformation before they reach the final consumer (e.g., raw cotton → yarn → cloth). (मध्यवर्ती वस्तुएं — आगे रूपांतरण की आवश्यकता)

 

• They are not counted directly in a country's GDP, to avoid the problem of double counting.

 

• Intermediate goods are consumed entirely within the same accounting year for further production.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Final goods (which include consumer goods and capital goods) are ready for final use and require no further transformation; only final goods are counted while computing national income.

 

NOTE

 

• Consumer durable goods (Option 1): Final goods used directly and repeatedly by consumers (e.g., refrigerators); need no further transformation.

 

• Finished goods (Option 2): By definition, are already processed and ready for final sale/use, not requiring further transformation.

 

• Capital goods (Option 4): Final goods (like machinery) used in the production process, not intermediate goods.

question: In which of the following states is the Nrityagram, an Odissi dance institution, located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nrityagram, an Odissi dance institution/village, is located near Hesaraghatta, Bengaluru, Karnataka. (नृत्यग्राम — कर्नाटक)

 

• It was founded by the dancer Protima Bedi in 1990, following a Gurukul-style residential system of training in Indian classical dance.

 

• Apart from Odissi, the institution also imparts training in other classical dance forms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nrityagram Dance Ensemble, currently led by Surupa Sen, performs internationally and is well known for its Odissi productions.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Known for institutions like Kerala Kalamandalam, associated with Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, not Nrityagram.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Known for various Bharatanatyam institutions, not Nrityagram.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Not the location of Nrityagram.

question: Who among the following was the youngest instrumentalist to be awarded the Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian award of India in 2002?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Zakir Hussain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain, the celebrated tabla maestro, was the youngest instrumentalist to be awarded the Padma Bhushan (India's third-highest civilian award) in 2002. (उस्ताद ज़ाकिर हुसैन — पद्म भूषण 2002)

 

• He is the son of the legendary tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha, and is regarded as one of the greatest tabla players in Hindustani classical music.

 

• He was later awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2023, India's second-highest civilian award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Bhushan is India's third-highest civilian award, ranking below the Bharat Ratna and Padma Vibhushan, and above the Padma Shri.

 

• Zakir Hussain also won multiple Grammy Awards for his collaborative work in world/classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (Option 1): A legendary sitar player and Bharat Ratna awardee (1999), but not the personality referred to here.

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (Option 3): A renowned Hindustani classical vocalist, not an instrumentalist, and a Bharat Ratna awardee (2008).

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (Option 4): A legendary shehnai player and Bharat Ratna awardee (2001), but not the youngest instrumentalist Padma Bhushan awardee of 2002.

question: Who was the revenue minister during the reign of Akbar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Todar Mal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Todar Mal served as the revenue minister in Emperor Akbar's court, and is credited with introducing the Zabti (Dahsala) land revenue settlement system. (राजा टोडरमल — अकबर के राजस्व मंत्री)

 

• He was one of the ‘Navratnas’ (nine gems) of Akbar's court.

 

• Under the Dahsala system, land revenue was fixed based on the average produce and prices of the previous ten years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Navratnas of Akbar's court included Birbal, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Tansen, Raja Man Singh, and Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana.

 

NOTE

 

• Abdul Rahim (Option 2): Known as Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana, a poet and military commander, and also a Navratna, but not the revenue minister.

 

• Mulla Do-Piyaza (Option 3): A legendary courtier figure of folklore, often paired with Birbal in popular stories, not a recognised revenue official.

 

• Tansen (Option 4): A legendary court musician and Navratna, unrelated to revenue administration.

question: Which of the following Illustrations shows the mitochondrion’s structural details?
solution_text:
The correct answer is b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Illustration ‘b’ correctly depicts the structural details of a mitochondrion — its outer membrane, folded inner membrane (forming cristae), and the matrix. (माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया की संरचना — चित्र b)

 

• Mitochondria are often called the ‘powerhouse of the cell’, since they are the site of ATP production through cellular respiration (Krebs cycle and electron transport chain).

 

• The cristae (folds of the inner membrane) increase the surface area available for the enzymes involved in respiration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mitochondria possess their own DNA (mtDNA) and ribosomes, which supports the endosymbiotic theory of their origin from free-living bacteria.

 

NOTE

question: Which of the following is a straight-chain alkyl carboxylic acid with the chemical formula CH3CH2CH2CO2H?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Butyric acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Butyric acid (Butanoic acid) is a straight-chain, saturated carboxylic acid with the formula CH3CH2CH2COOH (C4H8O2). (ब्यूटिरिक अम्ल — CH3CH2CH2CO2H)

 

• It is found in rancid butter and is responsible for its characteristic unpleasant, sour odour.

 

• It belongs to the homologous series of alkanoic (carboxylic) acids, being the fourth member of the series.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The homologous series of straight-chain carboxylic acids begins: Methanoic acid (C1) → Ethanoic acid (C2) → Propanoic acid (C3) → Butanoic acid (C4).

 

NOTE

 

• Methanoic acid (Option 1): Formula HCOOH (formic acid), the first (C1) member of the series.

 

• Propionic acid (Option 2): Also called propanoic acid, formula CH3CH2COOH, the third (C3) member.

 

• Ethanoic acid (Option 3): Also called acetic acid, formula CH3COOH, the second (C2) member.

question: Article 77 of the Indian Constitution deals with the __________.
option_1: term of office of the Vice-President
option_3: oath of office by the Vice-President
option_4: conduct of business of the Government of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is conduct of business of the Government of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 77 of the Indian Constitution deals with the ‘Conduct of business of the Government of India’. (अनुच्छेद 77 — भारत सरकार के कार्य संचालन)

 

• It provides that all executive action of the Union Government shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.

 

• Article 77(3) empowers the President to make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government and for the allocation of business among Ministers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 78 lays down the duties of the Prime Minister with respect to furnishing information to the President regarding decisions of the Council of Ministers.

 

NOTE

 

• Term of office of the Vice-President (Option 1): Covered under Article 67.

 

• Vice-President of India (Option 2): The office itself is established under Article 63.

 

• Oath of office by the Vice-President (Option 3): Covered under Article 69.

question: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 deals with subsistence allowance in which of the following Sections?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Section 5.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Section 5 of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 provides for subsistence allowance — a married Muslim woman on whom talaq is pronounced is entitled to seek an amount of subsistence allowance from her husband for herself and her dependent children. (धारा 5 — निर्वाह भत्ता)

 

• The Act makes the pronouncement of talaq-e-biddat (instant triple talaq) void and illegal (Section 3), and a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment up to three years along with a fine (Section 4).

 

• The amount of subsistence allowance is to be determined by a Magistrate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Section 6 of the Act entitles the woman to the custody of her minor children.

 

• Section 7 lays down conditions relating to the offence being compoundable and bailable, with bail granted by a Magistrate after hearing the wife.

 

NOTE

 

• Section 6 (Option 2): Deals with custody of minor children, not subsistence allowance.

 

• Section 7 (Option 3): Deals with bail and compounding of the offence, not subsistence allowance.

 

• Section 4 (Option 4): Deals with punishment for pronouncing talaq, not subsistence allowance.
